target_customer: Enterprises and blockchain developers needing encrypted data sharing and access control
problem: Sharing sensitive data between parties without trusting a central key manager or exposing plaintext.
business_model: Token-incentivized network with usage fees for re-encryption and access control services
product_category: Cryptographic infrastructure, proxy re-encryption and threshold access control

founders.name: MacLane Wilkison
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no professional history.

founders.name: Michael Egorov
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in one profile; cryptography lead for the project (single source).

exit.reason: Community votes in 2021 approved merging NuCypher and Keep into Threshold; NU and KEEP tokens were swapped for T.

technical_complexity.rationale: Proxy re-encryption with threshold splitting (the Umbral scheme) and a cryptoeconomic node network required research-grade cryptography and a novel token protocol.

defensibility.rationale: Original cryptographic primitives and a node operator network were hard to copy quickly, but open source code lowered the barrier for forks and rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; it merged with a peer protocol (Keep) in 2021.

market_need_then: In 2017 TechCrunch described NuCypher selling proxy re-encryption to enterprises with large sensitive datasets moving to the cloud, with the 2017 KMS paper arguing against trusting a key management provider.

identity.mascot_or_character: Alice and Bob style cast: Alice, Bob, Ursula (re-encryption nodes), Enrico (encryptor)

branding.brand_signature: Alice-and-Bob character narrative (Ursula nodes, Enrico) running through the codebase

rebrands.why: Merger with Keep Network; NuCypher's access control product became TACo (Threshold Access Control).

branding.community_and_virality: NU token and node operator community (144 node operators voted on the merger per one summary); no merch or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within crypto and cryptography circles, with a memorable cast of character names, but little evidence of broader recognition and the name was folded into Threshold.

outcome_analysis: NuCypher raised a 4.3M USD round in late 2017 and about 10.7M USD in October 2019 from crypto funds, built genuine cryptographic primitives and launched its network, then merged with Keep Network in 2021 to form Threshold. The crypto token boom helped fundraising, and the independent brand was absorbed. YC lists it as Inactive because the company folded into Threshold, not because of a reported failure.
notes: YC status Inactive conflicts with the live Threshold Network site; exit recorded as merger. One snippet reported a 133M USD valuation for the 2019 round; unverified so not recorded. A 2019 total of 15.8M USD is also from a single snippet. No dated competitor sources were found for 2016. The a16z and Pantera claims were not supported. The 2019 round was a SAFT with tokens, hence stage other.
